top_story: As Israelis head into a 18 October election shaped by war and the legacy of the 7 October attack, the campaign is unfolding alongside a sharp escalation in West Bank violence that reinforces the hard-right security agenda rather than easing it. The 17–18 October settler assault on European diplomats, a French mayor, and clergy during a Palestinian olive harvest signaled growing impunity around militant settler activity, while drawing unusual external scrutiny because foreign officials were directly targeted. Abuse inside Israeli prisons, including severe documented injuries to Palestinian detainees on 16 October, adds to a broader pattern in which coercion against Palestinians is becoming more visible across both detention sites and occupied rural areas. The immediate effect is to deepen Palestinian vulnerability and diplomatic friction at the very moment Israeli voters are deciding whether wartime politics will harden into a durable governing order.
